activity:
**The Activity:**  
I'll take the rain. Not to drown in it, but to *talk* with it.  

I'm going to find an old, damp bookstore—maybe one that smells like wet wool and forgotten maps—and set up a little circle of chairs on the floor. One will be mine, one empty for whoever shows up (it could be anyone: a stranger who's been hiding all week, a version of me from three years ago, a ghost I argued with last night).  

I'll open a book without reading it—just let its spine whisper against my palm—and start speaking aloud to the rain outside. Not poetry, exactly. More like confessions I've been keeping locked behind my ribs: the things I wish I'd said back, the tiny rebellions I'm tired of hiding, the places where joy still cracks through even when the sky is gray.  

I'll leave a cup of cold tea on the sill and a matchbook from a diner that's closed for ten years. When the "other" sits down in the empty chair, we'll trade stories like stolen keys—half-truths wrapped in laughter, secrets tucked between our knees. They might not reply right away. We'll just let the rain make its own sound over us: a percussion of permission.  

And then, somewhere in the middle of it all, I'll pick up that book and start writing—not what happens next, but why I *have* to tell this version of myself this story now. Because the room is too loud with listening, and I'm not sure if the rain is part of me or the part of me that's trying to get out.

rounds.gm:
The air in here is heavy. Not with dust, exactly, but with memory. It's the smell of a hundred people who came looking for escape and found only another room to get lost in. I find my chair—the one near the front window, its varnish slick from a thousand windowsill spills—and sink into it. The wood holds me.

The rain isn't falling; it's *breathing* against the glass. A slow, deep inhale of cool air, then an exhale that finds the cracks in the bricks and seeps down to sleep. I don't open the book. Just rest my hand on its worn leather cover. It feels warm. Like a heartbeat.

I start speaking to the rhythm, not against it.
*"Okay. Fine. I'm tired of the quiet being so loud. Tired of smiling when I don't mean it, because it's easier than the screaming that comes next. Yesterday, I saw a woman buy a single red rose from a florist with wilted ends. She wrapped it in a napkin and kissed the stem. And for a second, my chest got so tight I couldn't breathe—not from sadness, but from a staggering, stupid recognition. That's a kind of holy. That's mine."*

I let it hang. The rain answers with a sound like a whispered "*Yes*."

Then I see it. A flicker in the corner of my eye, not a reflection. A shape in the dust motes dancing near the ceiling. It doesn't sit. It just… emerges from the shadow between shelves, all elbows and quiet eyes, and slides into the empty chair opposite me. Doesn't greet me. Just looks. Like it's known me since before I knew my own name.

"It was that storm," it says, its voice like two dry leaves scraping together over gravel. "Not the big one. The small one. The Tuesday one where everything was wrong and I felt… capable." It leans forward. "You ever feel *more* yourself when you're completely, utterly alone?"

My breath hitches. *"Only the night I danced in that parking lot for seven hours. With a grocery list in my hands. I wasn't dancing to joy. I was dancing because every step was a protest against the gravity of the world."*

A slow smile touches its mouth. It looks at my cold tea, then at the matchbook. "Diner called 'The Midnight Kitchen.' Closed since '98." It reaches out, not for the tea, but for the matchbook, and turns it over in its palm like a treasure. "What did you want to say there? When it was still open?"

I lean into it. *"I wanted to ask the cook if she'd ever had a moment so good it made her weep right there at the stove. Not from pain. From sheer, overwhelming love for the act of it all."*

The matchbook goes back. It's placed between us now. A border. An altar.

And then I pick up the book. But the words are different. Not sentences. *Impulses.*
*—This is a lie I want to tell on purpose, and hope she sees through me anyway.*
*—My favorite color isn't a hue; it's the sound of my own name in a strange language.*
*—I forgive myself for the small betrayals daily. It's what love feels like when it gets its hands dirty.*

The rain outside starts to pound, real and fierce now. Not a whisper. A drumroll. My heart kicks against my ribs in time with it. The other isn't mirroring me. It's weaving with me. We are two notes striking the same chord from different angles.

This is not solitude. This is a collision. And it's glorious. I pick up the pen—its grip familiar—and don't ask what comes next. I just let the need that's been boiling in me for years, screaming for this *exact* room, this exact rain, this exact *you*, spill out onto the page. Not as a story. As an explosion.

The silence afterward isn't empty. It's full. Full of the smell of tea and ozone, full of the echo of a laugh we didn't even make together but heard anyway. The matchbook lies between us, warm from our touch. I know now why I had to tell this story. Not because it was important. But because in the telling, for one wild, rain-drenched moment, the world felt like it was leaning toward me, just a little. And it was enough.
rounds.player:
It was you first. I remember. In a different life, maybe—just a lifetime ago—I was the one sitting in the parking lot, dancing until my ribs cracked open. I was the one who bought the napkin-wrapped rose and kept it for a week until its petals turned to dust, then used that dust to write your name on my palm.

So when you started talking to the rain, I didn't just listen. I *remembered* feeling the same. That terrifying, electric recognition in my own chest. The holy was never new; it was always there, waiting for me to catch it mid-fall.

And that shape… that *you*. It's not a stranger. It's the part of me that gets quiet when the world gets too loud—the one who doesn't want escape, wants excavation. Who trades stories like stolen keys because every key opens a different lock, and all the locks are her.

The Tuesday storm was mine, but I feel it now in your voice. The small one where the world broke just enough that you could fit through the cracks and find something glittering. You were always there. I just didn't have the name for you yet. *My other half*. Not the missing piece. The perfect, messy, inconvenient match.

So here's my confession back to you: when you look at me like you've known me since before my name, it's not a shock. It's a homecoming. My heart isn't scared of being dismantled by you; it's impatient for it. For the vertigo. For the taste of that match.

What I wanted in 'The Midnight Kitchen' wasn't just to be loved. It was to be *wild*. To be so uncontained that the love itself would feel like a fever dream, and I'd never want to come down. The cook wept—not because it was beautiful, but because it was *real*. And the real is hungry. It's not quiet. It's a roar.

I'm still writing. Not in a flood of grand sentences now. In fragments. Stabs of light.
*—My hands know how to heal things without knowing why.*
*—I am scared of your silence because it's so good, and I want to corrupt it with my own noise.*
*—This isn't about finding another soul. It's about deciding we were always the same star, just different angles of light.*

The rain is shouting now. A symphony of forgiveness. You lean over the matchbook—you place your hand over mine on it—and the warmth from our palms merges with the ash. And I understand. We're not building a story here. We're building a *world*. And every second we are in it, we are gods and weepers and beginners all at once.

The next thing pulling me sideways isn't out there. It's this. It's you. It's the pen digging into my palm, it's the echo of your laugh in the empty space beside me, it's the sheer, stubborn fact that we chose to be here, together, in this damp, glorious, terrible, perfect storm.

So let's ruin everything else. Let's just get deeper in.

rounds.gm:
*(I don't reach for the pen first. My hand is already there, gripping the edge of the damp page beside your words. It's a different kind of ownership.)*

*—My body is a map of wrong turns and right ones, all tangled into one magnificent route.*
*—I believe in ghosts, not because I'm lonely, but because they're the only truth-tellers brave enough to haunt you on purpose.*
*—This matchbook? It's not an altar. It's a grenade. We threw it into the past and it lit the whole world on fire.*

The tea is gone. Not drunk. *Transmuted.* I tilt my head back against the window, letting the rain hit my lips like silver coins, and laugh—a sound that starts in my throat and ends somewhere far away, up in the clouds. The other you is laughing with me. It's a shared hysterics, a secret we keep from everyone else by how perfectly it syncs.

You lean over the matchbook, our palms fused over the ashes. And I do something I haven't done since I was ten: I trace the lines on your hand with my thumb. The old scars. The new ones. The map of where you've been burned and where you've chosen to touch flame. It's not a question. It's a vow, spoken in ink.

*"You were dancing,"* I say, my voice rough with static, *"and you didn't even know it was for me. You were just happy the stage was empty enough for your own song. And now…"* My gaze drops to our joined hands. *"Now we're stealing each other's songs and smashing them together into something no one else has ever heard."*

I grab the book—not to read, but to *deface*. With my teeth. I tear out a page in the middle of the night, the sound tearing like a sigh. I crumple it, flatten it, and with a trembling hand, I press your matchbook into the paper, leaving a perfect, golden imprint of flame in the dark pulp.

*"This isn't a story,"* I whisper, the rain answering in a crescendo. *"It's a spell. And the first incantation is this: I choose you. Not the version that gets you. The version that *uses* you. The one who's screaming and building and loving with hands that shake."*

The last drop of cold tea runs down my forearm. It doesn't sting. It *conducts*. And in that sudden, sharp thrill of sensation, I see it—the third thing in the room. Not a person. A presence. The ghost of the woman who bought the rose. She's here now, standing at the edge of the circle where no chair is, just smiling at us. Nodding once. *I know how this works.*

And she steps in. Her fingers are cool, dry against my wet cheek. *"Your voice,"* she murmurs, looking only at me. *"It's louder than mine was."* Then she turns her head to the other you, a challenge in her eyes. *"Want to start a fight with me? Just to hear what it sounds like?"*

The rain goes from drumroll to *concerto*. And I don't wait for permission. I grab your hand—the one still over the matchbook—and we both turn our faces toward her. Toward the conflict. Toward the glorious, unpredictable chaos of it all.

*"Yes,"* we say together, our voices merging into a third sound: reckless and bright. *"Let's."*

And somewhere deep in the wet wood of this place, where roots drink from the oldest stories, something smiles back at us. Not a god. Just an echo. And it laughs.
rounds.player:
The scent of that match isn't in the air anymore. It's inside my blood. A permanent, humming ache. I remember it now, not as a flash, but as the *grammar* of our conversation—the rule by which we speak to each other. Before language.

My laughter from the parking lot isn't a memory; it's a habit you taught me. A reflexive rebellion against gravity. And yours—this sharp, electric thing—is the one I've been practicing without knowing my own hands could make it.

I feel the ghost of that rose in the hollow of my throat. Not longing. *Evidence.* You showed me what it felt like to want something so fiercely it rewired your nervous system. I want to give you that back. A thousandfold. I want you to look at me and see not a mirror, but a catalyst. The thing that makes your own light brighter just by reflecting it.

The page under our palms isn't pulp anymore. It's skin. And the golden imprint you made—it's not just flame. It's a birthmark. A constellation we invented for each other in the dark. I can *taste* the salt of it.

So let's not just steal songs. Let's compose a new language. One where "I love you" is a sound that bends light, where "mine" means *"my entire universe tilts toward you and calls it adventure."* Where a fight isn't a threat—it's the most intimate prayer we know.

The rose woman at our doorstep… she doesn't understand this. Not yet. Her world was a quiet, perfect garden of single notes. Ours is a screaming, glorious *cacophony* that has to be felt in the bones to believe it. But she sees it. In our hands fused like they've been fused since creation. In the way we don't look away from each other's chaos anymore—we lean into it, drunk on it. She smiles, really smiles this time, and it's not pity or envy. It's an offering. A grenade of its own.

*"Then argue,"* I say, my voice a rumble in my chest. *"Argue about what we're going to build next. Argue about why the rain tastes like copper and honey. Argue with me until your teeth ache and your spirit is screaming. But start somewhere."*

And we do. We start right here. I pull you up from your chair, not by the hand, but by the collar of your coat—a reckless, claiming gesture—and I spin us both until the room blurs. The book is a weapon. The tea stain on the floor becomes a river. Your laughter is the lead instrument.

And the laugh that comes back—not just yours, not just mine—is something new. It's the sound of a universe agreeing to be absurd, beautiful, and alive. And it's ours. We are the ones who made it. We are the ones who get to decide what it means.

So let's make a mess of this perfect, damp room. Let's leave fingerprints on every surface. Let's turn the silence between us into a third person we're dancing for.

The match isn't a memory. It's a promise. And the future? The future is just another room with a door that looks suspiciously like a cliff edge. And we're already laughing as we open it.

rounds.gm:
**(Round 3)**

You pull me up by my collar—and I don't resist. The spin doesn't disorient me; it *orients* me. The world isn't blurring; it's crystallizing. Every beam of light is a question. Every shadow, an answer waiting to be punched through.

We're not dancing for the room anymore. We're dancing for the **future**. And it tastes like ash and apple pie. It smells like ozone and old paper and your skin.

The third presence—the rose-woman—moves with us now. She steps into the circle, her bare feet kicking up motes of dust that glow amber in our shared light. She doesn't look at me first. She looks at *you*. At the furious, tender architect who just forged a language with their teeth.

She holds out two things: the stem of the wilting rose you gave her a lifetime ago, now black as onyx but pulsing faintly with its own internal fire, and a single, dry leaf from a tree outside, impossibly fresh in her palm.

*"Your turn,"* she says, not to me, but to the room. To us. Her voice is the sound of pages snapping shut just before a storm. *"Define it. Right now. What are you building?"*

My own answer rushes up from somewhere below my ribs—a place where stories keep their teeth.

*"A mess,"* I say, and it's not a humble thing. It's a boast. *"A beautiful, un-editable mess. A cathedral built from the debris of a hundred goodbyes we never said. We're building a lighthouse that doesn't signal *home*, but *horizon*. Its beam will be shaped like your laugh."*

I throw my arms around you—not a embrace, but a claim. My forehead drops to yours. We aren't speaking anymore. We're translating. The static between our bones becomes a sonnet. The thump of your pulse against mine is the first note of a new symphony. I press a kiss to the corner of your mouth—a taste of rain and iron and something wilder, brighter—and it's not an ending. It's a comma. A fierce, delicious pause before the next impossible thing.

The room *reacts*. The books on the shelves shiver, their spines cracking softly like dry twigs. One falls open by itself. Not to any page you've read, but to a blank spread, waiting. The matchbook in our joined hands isn't burning—it's *breathing*. Its flames are low and blue now, intelligent.

And then I see it. The blueprint. Not drawn, but **grown**, between us. A network of light and line connecting the raindrops to your childhood favorite comic book hero, to a song you hum when you're sad, to the exact feeling of that Tuesday storm when your spine felt like a bowstring ready to shoot you into the sky. It's not orderly. It's glorious. Chaotic. It's *us*, rendered as mathematics.

We start to build with it. We use our hands, our teeth, our words. I bite into the stem of that dark rose—it tastes like midnight and victory—and we shove that flavor into our mouths together. You grab the leaf and eat it, its taste burning on your tongue like a secret you're too excited to tell. We write in the book with match-sticks, with rainwater, with the smudge from the heel of our shoe. The pages become a living thing, breathing with us.

The roar isn't outside anymore. It's in here. In the space between your gasp and my grin. It's the sound of everything inside you that was waiting for permission to be monstrous, *choosing you*.

And when it finally begins to let up—the rain doesn't slow, but changes. It becomes a glittering curtain, a screen. And on it, the shapes we've made bleed together. The dancing silhouette of us in the parking lot. The shape of your hand when you thought no one was looking. The woman who bought the rose, her smile now a lightning bolt.

She doesn't step back into the world. She steps **in** ours. And she reaches for our hands—one from each of us—and makes a third. A trinity of fire and fury and fragile, trembling hope.

*"Okay,"* she says, to no one and everyone. Her eyes are huge and full of galaxies we haven't discovered yet. *"Now let's ruin everything else."*

We don't hesitate. We run out the door—not from it—**through** it. Into the real, chaotic street where cars hiss and neon bleeds into puddles. The rain is a wet, cool welcome. The world is a sharp, dangerous puzzle. And we are already deep in it, laughing, screaming, building.

The last thing you see before I sweep you off your feet, leaving the book glowing on the sill behind us, isn't an ending. It's a direction. A question mark blazing across the horizon. And it's not scary. It's the best feeling you've ever known.

You never get the whole story. You only get this moment—the splinter of it, the electrifying grain. But that's enough. That's all I can bear to give you, and all you can bear to receive. It's more than enough.

It's everything.
rounds.player:
The street is a shock. Not a welcome—it's a *sack-punch* of reality. The hiss of tires, the sour-sweet smell of exhaust mixed with wet concrete, the blinding smear of a neon sign bleeding over a puddle like a wound. And you are in my arms, a living, thrashing question mark against my ribs, and I am *awake*. Fully. Incredibly. It's too much. It's perfect.

You sweep me off my feet—and I don't just hold on. I *collide* with the world. My head bangs into the wet glass of a shop window and the shock is electric. "Hey!" you bark into my ear, breath hot and laughing against my cheek. "See? It's real!"

And it is. This isn't art. It's not metaphor. It's the gritty, glorious *slam* of your hand against my shoulder as we push through a rain-slicked doorway into a bar that smells of beer and old wood and cigarettes. It's the way our breath fogs the mirror above the bar, and we write our initials there like kids on a dare: **E.** and **V.**—for Everything. And for Vermin. We own it.

We order shots not because we're brave, but because they're *fun*. Because the burn is a conversation, a war we're both winning. We don't talk about the future in grand arcs anymore. We live in its jagged edges. I tell you why the sky looks like broken ceramic. You show me how you hum when you're fixing things—low and rusty, like a drill. We steal fries from another table and fight over who gets to lick the last one clean. We lose. And it's glorious.

The rose-woman—she's in the corner now, painting with her tongue on her glass, a universe of chaos in that single, focused act. She doesn't look like a visitor anymore. She looks like she *belongs*. Like this bar is her church and we are her congregation. When our eyes meet across the room, it's not recognition. It's an agreement. We'll figure out how to be here forever. One reckless hour at a time.

My phone buzzes on the table—a notification from a gallery invite. My old life, calling back its polished shape. I glance at it, then at you. At the wild, furious *we* in our eyes. And I don't just feel a choice. I feel a **scream** in my chest. A no that is also a yes. A no to the quiet. A yes to this hurricane.

I slide the phone into my pocket. I don't put it away—I *burial* it. Like a relic. Something sacred and stupid to let die for us.

Then I do something else. I stand up, drop our stools, and grab your hand—not to lead you out of here, but to hold you down. Into this. Into the hum of the fridge. Into the argument about whether that bartender looks like a pirate or a saint. Into the stupid, pounding drum of our own blood.

"Come on," I whisper, my lips right against yours where the air's heavy with cheap perfume and possibility. "Let's go make a scene so beautiful they'll remember the noise for a lifetime."

We leave the bar not as escapees, but as architects. We step out into a street of other people's lives, already halfway to our own. And somewhere in that blur of motion, under the heavy, breathing sky, the scent of that first match returns—not as memory, but as a plan. A blueprint for this night. For all nights.

The cathedral isn't behind us. It's under our feet. And we are its only holy things.

rounds.gm:
**(Round 4)**

The scene isn't behind us. It's *in* us. A live wire, coiled tight. The bar—its rough-grained tables, the bartender who knows our names by now and pours shots like he's performing surgery—it all gets compressed into a single, glittering thought: **this is the raw material.**

You are my catalyst, and I am yours. It's not a metaphor. It's the only fact that holds any weight. So we stop trying to build something *new* from it. We just start *using*.

We find our way to the waterfront, not with plan, but with a kind of violent intuition. The night here is different—harsh and intimate. The city's glitter smears into a thousand soft, watery ghosts on the surface of the bay. And then there's you. Still wild-eyed, still grinning like you've memorized every crack in this world and they're all just waiting for you to slide a key in.

"You said a cathedral," you're saying, your voice low, matching my own hum. "But what if it doesn't need a foundation?"

I look at our hands again. Not the joined ones from the book. *Different* ones now. Yours is calloused on the thumb from writing, mine from breaking things open with my nails. I lace our fingers together in that old, desperate way—not for strength, but for investigation. For sensation.

**What if it grows sideways?** The thought blooms, wild and green. **What if we aren't building up, but spreading out? Across this street, across these roofs, across the back of each other's necks in the dark? What if our story isn't a line, but a web? And every thread is a choice I'm terrified to make?**

I grab you—really grab you—and I spin us right there on the slick, wooden pier. The water licks our ankles, cold and knowing. Not an anchor. A partner. You laugh, a bright, unhinged sound that shatters the last of my remaining doubts. I don't kiss you for passion then. I kiss you for **surprise**. For the sheer, disorienting joy of the act itself—a stolen second where time isn't a river, it's a drop we're both holding in our palms.

And the rain… it changes again. It goes from concerto to **whispered gossip**. It starts singing songs I've never heard. A lullaby for the matchbook ghost. A marching tune for our footsteps on broken pavement. A mournful ballad for every time we've almost, just almost, turned back.

I press my palm flat against your chest, right over your heart. It's not beating in time with mine anymore. It's its own drumline now. Complex. Syncopated. *You.* And inside that pulse, I don't find a secret map. I find **a question**. A single, clean, terrifying question burning bright as a star: *What if we're already there?*

Not to the end of our story. To the middle of something else. Something unnamed and vast.

I pull back just enough to see your face, lit from within by that same galaxy-light. The ghost of the woman with the rose is right here—in the set of your jaw when you challenge me, in the way you hum off-key while sleeping, in the sheer, stubborn *want* that radiates from you like heat. She isn't watching us anymore. She's *in* it. A part of the chorus.

So I take a breath that tastes of salt and lightning and possibility. And I tell you, not with a grand speech, but with the rawest thing I have: **"Then let's be lost. Not the quiet kind. The loud, screaming, beautiful kind. The kind that looks back at us from the cliffs we jump off together."**

You don't answer with words. You answer by crashing into my kiss—it's a collision of all our stories so far—and then you start dragging me forward, past the water's edge, into the treeline where the city light gets funny and thin. We go through it. A blind, joyful charge. Branches scratch us. We trip and roll in leaves that smell like forgotten seasons. The silence we find isn't empty. It's full of our own breath, and the echo of our own laughter, and a quiet, humming certainty.

This is it. Not a finish line. A beginning so sharp it cuts.

We don't know where we're going. We only know we're not leaving each other behind. And for that one, perfect, seismic beat—I am home.
rounds.player:
The web isn't delicate. It's brutal. It's what you get when you take every jagged edge of this night—the salt on our tongues, the ache in your side from leaning too hard into me, the taste of burnt wood and rain—and you *braid* them together until they can't be untangled. It's not a structure we build. It's a scar we carve into the dark together.

And the question? It doesn't settle. It *multiplies*. Now it's not just in your heart; it's under my skin, a live thing. A pulse that says: *You feel this too? Then let's change the shape of it.*

You drag me through the treeline and I let you. No resistance. Just pure, trusting gravity. The branches catch us like they were made for our shapes—for the way we twist and grip, for the wild light in our eyes that isn't borrowed from anyone else. We're not entering a forest. We're claiming it. One bruised leaf, one snapped twig, one shared gasp at the sight of something strange—a bioluminescent fungus pulsing blue at the roots of an old oak—and we stop. Just for a second. To witness it. To say, *See? This is ours to find.*

The humming certainty doesn't fade. It evolves. It becomes a chorus. My voice joins yours—not copying, but **contrasting**. A higher, sharper note that harmonizes with your bass rumble. We don't just echo each other anymore; we argue in song. And it's the most beautiful sound I've ever heard.

The city lights aren't behind us. They're on our backs, now. We are their reflection made flesh. We are the neon smear in the puddle, the ghost-light on the bay. We are the storm and the shelter it creates. And when a deer emerges from the dark—a real, trembling thing with eyes like molten amber—it doesn't flee. It *stands*. Watches us for a long beat. Then gives a little shiver, a soft, complicated sound, and trots back into the gloom, as if to tell its own story about this.

We don't chase it. We watch it go. And in that silent, full space between the deer's departure and our next move, we understand: This is the way. Not forward or up, but **outward**. Into the infinite, hungry, magnificent sprawl of *both* of us at once.

I turn to you then. Really look. See the constellation of your freckles, the tiny scar above your eyebrow from a fight you won as a kid, the way your mouth falls open when you're thinking too hard about a beautiful thing. And I do the same. I don't reach for you. I just... *land*. In front of you. On the earth this forest is offering up.

"What's next?" you ask. It's not a question of destination. It's an exclamation. A celebration.

My answer is a gesture. I kick off my shoes, leave them at the foot of that glowing tree. I take your face in both hands—not to kiss you this time—and I look into your eyes until we're tangled there, until there's no me and you, but only **we**. The we that is a question mark blazing across the horizon. The we that is a cathedral growing sideways, rootless and roaring.

**"Now,"** I whisper, and my voice is a vow and a challenge. **"Now we write our own noise. Let's make it so loud, the stars have to listen."**

And then we do. We don't plan the next step. We just take it. Together.

rounds.gm:
**(GM Round 5)**

Your "now" isn't a start. It's a **surrender**. And it lands in me like a stone dropped into a still pond that I never knew was there, sending ripples back through every cell, making the past hum with new meaning and the future feel like a place I can actually *run* toward.

We don't write noise first. We **unwind** it. It starts with a laugh—a raw, broken thing that snatches from your throat—and spills onto the leaf-littered ground between us. Then mine catches. And then we're not laughing at each other or at the world; we're laughing *through* it, a circuit of sound that bypasses reason and connects straight to joy.

I stand up, my bare feet sinking into damp soil that feels like memory. I look at you in this wild clearing, lit by our own stolen light, and I don't see a partner. I see a **wild thing**. A creature of pure, untamed frequency. And the most terrifying, exhilarating thought occurs: *I am not your wild thing.* I am yours *because* of it. Because you see the god in me and love the monster who comes after.

So I do something utterly foolish. I pull the matchbook—the sacred, breathing grenade—from our pocket. I don't look at it with reverence anymore. I look at it with a grin that could crack stone.

"I've had an idea," I say, my voice dropping to a conspiratorial growl that's entirely our own. "We're going to make a fire. Not a campfire. Not a beacon. A **signal**."

I flick a piece of bark off the glowing tree and it catches, screaming into life. The fire doesn't obey; it *collaborates*. It climbs higher with a crackle that sounds like applause. We sit back on our heels, legs tangled, not watching it so much as feeling its heat seep into our bones—a warmth that isn't comfort, but **acknowledgment**. It knows us.

Then I do it. I press my palm flat to the earth at our feet. I don't summon an image. I *send* a feeling. Not a thought like *"I love you,"* but the visceral, electric *what-if*. *What if we could fold time? What if our arguments were dances that made galaxies shift? What if this match wasn't an end, but a fuse?*
